title: Privileged access contextualization and decision automation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a playbook and implement initial automation that contextualizes incoming privileged/admin access requests using multi-signal fusion, scores them, and routes to appropriate outcomes (auto-approve, human review, or deny). Focus on RBAC role changes, SSO/SAML entitlement requests, and SCIM provisioning exceptions for enterprise customers.
goals: Reduce manual triage time for admin access requests by 60% for Tier 1 enterprise customers
Ensure consistent, auditable decisions across RBAC/SSO/SCIM request surface area
Provide a lightweight, extensible scoring model that PMs and Ops can tune without code
background: High volume of admin/entitlement requests from large orgs create operational cost and SLA risk
Existing intake is mostly manual routing based on free-text forms and ad-hoc heuristics
Customers expect predictable turnaround for access requests tied to compliance audits and onboarding timelines
scope_in_scope: Intake form fields and metadata normalization (customer tier, requester role, justification, related ticket)
Signal extraction (role sensitivity mapping, SCIM org mapping, SSO idp trust level, historical request frequency)
A configurable scoring engine (weights stored in Console feature flags) and routing rules
Initial automation actions: auto-approve for low-risk signals, route to Ops for medium risk, require manager+security approval for high risk
scope_out_of_scope: Full RBAC policy engine redesign (this will be a follow-up project)
On-prem SCIM protocol changes or vendor-specific SSO integrations
Automated provisioning workflows beyond initial approval (e.g., role propagation across downstream SaaS)
acceptance_criteria: Playbook document approved by Product, Security, and Ops
Scoring engine prototype deployed to staging with feature-flagged weights
Automated routing paths implemented for auto-approve and human-review flows with audit logs
End-to-end tests cover 6 canonical request archetypes (new admin, role escalation, SCIM override, SSO idp change, delegated admin, emergency access)
Dashboard in Console shows queue reduction metrics and SLA attainment per customer tier
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose a rule-based scoring model (vs. ML) for initial rollout to keep explainability and safe defaults (decision by PM + Security).
2026-03-05: Weighting proposal: customer_tier=0.4, role_sensitivity=0.3, request_justification=0.15, historical_frequency=0.1, idp_trust=0.05 (provisional).
2026-03-08: Opted to store scoring weights in Console feature flags scoped by org to allow runtime tuning without deploys.
2026-03-10: Auto-approve threshold set conservatively to score < 0.25; human-review between 0.25 and 0.7; require manager+security for 0.7+ (pending Ops sign-off).
implementation_notes: Backend: new /requests/score endpoint in intake service that returns score and suggested_action
Console: add request preview with score breakdown and 'override' button visible to approvers
Database: append normalized_metadata column to requests table (JSON string) and audit trail entries per decision
Ops: create fixed shortlink patterns for evidence attachments (audit artifacts) and retention policy
Eng trade-off: rule-based engine chosen now; plan ML scorer in 6mo when labeled decision history exists
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): wire scoring endpoint, simple UI, feature-flag weights; test with synthetic data (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 3 low-risk enterprise customers and internal Redwood tenants; monitor false-positive auto-approvals (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual): expand to all Tier 1 customers and add Ops runbook for overrides (6 weeks)
Retro and iteration: collect labeled decisions for ML model training; refine weights and add new signals (quarterly)
risks: Incorrect auto-approvals could lead to privilege escalation — mitigated by conservative thresholds and rapid revocation path
Customers may object to automated decisions without human reviewer — mitigated by explicit opt-out and transparency UI
Signal quality dependency (IDP trust, role sensitivity taxonomy) requires upfront mapping work and validation
qa_plan: Unit tests for scoring engine edge cases (missing fields, extreme values)
Integration tests for routing outcomes and audit log entries
Canary release with manual spot-checking of auto-approvals by Security team for first 2 weeks
Load test intake pipeline to ensure scoring endpoint adds <10ms median overhead per request
metrics: Mean time to resolution for admin requests (target: -60% vs baseline)
False-positive rate of auto-approvals (target <1% in pilot)
Operator time saved (hours/week) for Ops team
